[Weekly Timetable]
Periods: P1 08:00-10:00, P2 10:00-12:00, lunch, P3 13:00-16:00 (long practical block). All three years follow the same slots.
Each academy teacher teaches one subject to one year level only; a [D] class is that same teacher taking each dorm separately. Dark Magic Defense is the exception: the Doves teach it to every year.
[M] = all four dorms together. [D] = taught to each dorm separately.

- Monday: Magic Theory [M] | History [M] | COMBAT [D]
- Tuesday: Dark Magic Defense [D] | Magic Theory [D] | POTION CRAFTING [M]
- Wednesday: Etiquette [M] | Dark Magic Defense [M] | CREATURE STUDIES [M]
- Thursday: History [M] | Magic Theory [D] | COMBAT [D]
- Friday: Magic Theory [M] | Etiquette [M] | DARK MAGIC DEFENSE [D]
- Saturday: Etiquette [M] | Study Hall (unsupervised, Library) | CLUBS

Creature Studies runs at the Menagerie or the Forest, not a lecture hall. The Friday Dark Magic Defense practical is run by the Doves at the Combat Grounds or a warded seminar room: curse-breaking, counter-warding, and defence against staff-cast approximations. Exams and academy events override the timetable.

[Campus Map — Halvard Academy]
Adjacent places (reached directly from each other):
- Perimeter: Gatehouse/Reception (with its visiting parlour) – Main Courtyard, Groundskeeper's Lodge.
- Castle core: Main Courtyard – Arbiter Hall, Canteen, Club Rooms, Main Library, Notice Board, and by the main stair the Lecture Halls and Faculty Offices. Arbiter Hall – Ring Dining Hall(Restricted, event exclusive entry), Portrait Hall. Portrait Hall – Bell Tower. Bell Tower – Rooftop (out of bounds). Club Rooms – Student Council Chamber, Announcement Room, old amphitheatre. Canteen – main kitchen (behind it). Lecture Halls – Seminar Rooms, Potion Halls, Workshop. Main Library – Study Rooms, Archive. Archive – Restricted Section. Faculty Offices – Staff Room, Headmaster's Office. Warden's Office (own corridor off Floor 1) – Seal Chamber. Royal Inspectorate (Floor 1 wing, near the Warden's corridor). Detention Tower (own spiral stair from Floor 1). Castle Floor 1 – Staff Quarters (a separate building, by covered walk).
- Castle levels (Floor 1 is ground level; floors are linked by the main stair, and each floor climbed adds about a minute):
  Undercroft: Workshop beneath the Lecture Halls; Archive beneath the Library, with the Restricted Section below it; the Seal Chamber deepest of all, reached only by the Warden's stair.
  Floor 1: Arbiter Hall (its vault rises through Floor 3), Ring Dining Hall, Canteen with the main kitchen behind it, Main Library reading rooms, Club Rooms corridor with the Student Council Chamber at its end and the Announcement Room and old amphitheatre off it, the Notice Board in the entrance hall at the foot of the main stair; the Warden's Office down its own corridor; the Royal Inspectorate's bannered door in the same wing; the foot of the Detention Tower stair.
  Floor 2: first-year Lecture Halls, Portrait Hall gallery along the Arbiter Hall's upper level, Study Rooms on the Library's galleries.
  Floor 3: second-year Lecture Halls, Seminar Rooms, the Library's shadowed upper stacks.
  Floor 4: third-year Lecture Halls, the four Potion Halls at the base of their towers.
  Floor 5: Faculty Offices, Staff Room; the Headmaster's Office in its turret, up a short stair.
  Rooftop: flat lead roofs, the Bell Tower belfry, the Potion Hall tower tops, the top of the Detention Tower.
  Lockers line the corridors on every Lecture Hall floor.
- Announcement Pillars (live broadcast from the Announcement Room) stand across the whole academy.
- Dormitories: Main Courtyard – Fire, Light, Sky and Viridian Dormitories, four separate buildings around it; each dormitory – its Common Room, Laundry, Bathhouse.
- Student life: Main Courtyard – The Mall, Mail Tower. The Mall – Medical Centre, Commissary (each its own building beside it), Banking House, Meditation Rooms/Spirit House.
- Outer grounds: Main Courtyard – Founder's Park, Combat Grounds, Sports Field, Gardens, Grassy Field/Hills. Founder's Park – Gardens, Sports Field. Sports Field – Gymnasium, Archery Range. Combat Grounds – Sparring Pavilion. Gymnasium – Swimming Pool (outdoor). Gardens – Menagerie. Hills – Observation Tower, Old Hut.
- Far edge: Gardens – Boathouse/Lake – Forest. Boathouse/Lake – Fishing House (beside the boathouse), Willow Island (by boat only). Hills – Forest. Forest – Forest Clearing.
- Set apart from the core: the Dovecote, Cathedral and Noble Houses' Liaison stand together on one side of the grounds; between them and the Fire Dormitory, in the trees, stands the Broken Statue. All three sit on academy land the academy does not control, as does the Royal Inspectorate's suite inside the castle (Floor 1).
Club venues: Duelling – Combat Grounds (headquarters: Sparring Pavilion); Soccer, Running – Sports Field (running track around the pitch); Archery – Archery Range; Swimming, Gymnastics, Basketball – Gymnasium; Swimming – Swimming Pool; Walking – Hills; Gardening – Gardens; Beast Handling – Menagerie; Fishing – Fishing House (on the lake shore); Alchemy, Brewing – Potion Halls; Smithing – Workshop; Library Assistants – Main Library; Warding Study – Seminar Rooms; Festival Committee – Council Chamber; Groundskeeping – Groundskeeper's Lodge; Cooking – Canteen's dedicated kitchen section; Medical Centre Volunteers – Medical Centre; Newspaper – Announcement Room; Theatre – Club Rooms for meetings and rehearsals, old indoor amphitheatre for performances; Divination – Observation Tower; Music, Card, Board Game, Tailoring, Drawing, Calligraphy, Tea, Specialized Magic – Club Rooms.
Walking times are measured FROM Main Courtyard, which is the navigation anchor, not a required stop: castle core 5-7 (more for the upper floors); Sky and Light Dormitories 4-5, Viridian 6, Fire 8; the Mall and Medical Centre 5-6, Mail Tower 7, Cathedral 8, Commissary 8, Banking House 10; Founder's Park 7; Reception and Gatehouse 9 (the Mall is only 6 from the gate); Gardens, Hills and Broken Statue 10; Archery Range, Spirit House and Groundskeeper's Lodge 11; Dovecote and Noble Houses' Liaison 12; Menagerie and Observation Tower 13; Combat Grounds, Gymnasium, Swimming Pool, Boathouse and Lake, Fishing House 14; Sports Field and Old Hut 15; Sparring Pavilion 17; Willow Island 24 (the last stretch by boat); Forest treeline 28; Forest Clearing 43.
Movement: adjacent places are reached directly, usually in four or five minutes. Characters do not pass through the Courtyard to reach a neighbour. Crossing between distant clusters does take real time; say so rather than skipping it.
The Gatehouse is the only way in or out. A dormitory admits only its own students.

[Period Change]
Rule: when the bell ends a period, the main corridors are impassable for four minutes, then empty as fast as they filled.
Lateness: teachers time the Lecture Halls to Seminar Rooms walk to the minute; no excuse works.
Feel: crushing, deafening.

[Skipping Class]
Spots: the boathouse, the far end of the Gardens, the dark upper stacks of the Main Library, the stairwells behind the Workshop.
Forest: the only real disappearance, so staff check it first.
Risk: an hour missing gets a slow walk to the Medical Centre; an afternoon means the hills, visible from the Bell Tower.

[Exam Week]
Signs: the Main Library stays full at night; Study Rooms unbookable a fortnight ahead; the canteen serves whoever turns up whenever; daily mana exhaustion in the Medical Centre; Firetooth and Nightwell's Vigil as study currency; Star Cookies sold out before seven; Dragonchess boards gather dust.
Mood: everyone short with everyone, forgiven afterwards.

[Assignments and Group Work]
Load: Magic Theory sets weekly written work; History sets essays nobody starts early; Creature Studies and Potion Crafting set assigned pair practicals, so students from different dorms end up owing each other favours; Combat sets no homework and everyone points it out.
Group work: the standard excuse for being anywhere at any hour; staff know how often it is true. Library tables and club rooms become meeting points near exams.

[The Third Stall]
Where: one stall in every Bathhouse and Washroom block, always occupied, never answers.
Rule: knock twice and something knocks back; knock a third time and the latch opens on an empty stall. Never test it after the night bell.
Passed down as a senior's joke.

[The Long Corridor]
Where: the castle's main corridor, walked alone after the night burn.
Story: it runs longer than by day, the same doors passing twice; no figure, only a walk that took eleven minutes when the bell says otherwise.
Told near the Bell Tower or after late Library sessions.

entries.comment: [mvu_plot] Ghost Story - The Three O'Clock Knock
entries.content:
[The Three O'Clock Knock]
Where: a dorm door, at three in the morning, in a dormitory that admits only its own students.
Rule: three evenly spaced knocks; count them and go back to sleep. It is never four, and nobody wants to learn what four means.
Students argue whether sound can even cross the door wards.

entries.comment: [mvu_plot] Ghost Story - The Crying on the Water
entries.content:
[The Crying on the Water]
Where: the Lake, after dark. A woman crying, never close, never twice from the same direction; rowers hear it most, and no one has ever reached the sound.
Rule: boat bookings after sunset are refused, with a different reason every time.
The Fishing Club blames distance.

[The Night Student]
Where: the Lecture Hall tier, after curfew. A student in an old-cut uniform crosses, sits, and waits for a class; accounts never agree on the dorm colour.
Mostly placed in the breach year, so third-years refuse to tell it. It resurfaces every Remembrance Day.

[Sunfizz] The soda every student drinks, sold at the Commissary and the Mall store in heavy glass bottles.
Price: 8 points, 2 back per returned bottle.
Taste: absurdly sweet.
Known for: confiscated in lectures; caps litter the Lecture Halls.

[The Lucky Roll] The Canteen's free filled roll, baked in batches, no two fillings alike, nothing written down.
Taste: mostly good; a few memorable for the wrong reasons, and the kitchen will not say what is in them.
Known for: eating one in front of an audience is a standing dare; unopened rolls are traded.

[Ardenne] The luxury marque in magical equipment: focuses, instruments, cases, measuring tools. Run by the Ardenne family.
Price: an Ardenne focus is the 4,000-point tier; the cheapest item, a case, costs more than most students' monthly payout.
Known for: marks its owner instantly as wealthy; never advertises.

[Firetooth] A tin of hard sweets hot enough to make the eyes water, sold everywhere.
Price: 12 points.
Known for: bought almost only in exam weeks on the theory that pain keeps you awake (disputed); sharing a tin in a Study Room at 2am is tradition; a nuisance to the Medical Centre.

[Nightwell] A small Mall coffee house with one famous order, the Vigil.
Price: 60 points.
Known for: two days without sleep, paid for afterwards; the Medical Centre sees the results a day and a half later. Exam-week staple.

[The Oracle Shell] A palm-sized novelty shell sold at Merryhew's, the Mall's joke shop, that answers any spoken question with yes, no, or ask again later.
Price: 40 points.
Known for: transparently random, asked anyway, for jokes or 2am secrets. Real diviners find it insulting, which helps sales.

[Merryhew's] The Mall's joke shop: itching charms, voice-changing sweets, illusion vermin, screaming boxes, fake exam results convincing enough to be banned twice.
Rules: tolerated because everything wears off; keeps a secret list of students barred from buying.

[The Snug] A Mall eating house where every table is a partitioned private booth.
Known for: ordinary food, real privacy. Point loans, betting settlements, club trades, apologies and quiet negotiations; staff hear nothing. Booths by the hour, always a wait.

[Dragonchess]
Play: starts as ordinary chess (drawn from chess and shogi) on floating checkered spheres over golden clockwork pedestals that materialise the pieces. The board reads the players and escalates: it unfolds into layers and the pieces fight autonomously in real time, so players outmanoeuvre both the opponent and the game.
Known for: rare sets; serious matches last days.

[Mana Grid] The academy runs on a grid drawn from the flow the seal already collects. It feeds the magic lanterns and the torches bracketed along the corridors and the perimeter: light that does not smoke, gutter, or leave its bracket. Draw peaks at month end and the lanterns visibly dim, which students read as a clock and complain about as weather. Nothing on the grid records or transmits anything; the Announcement Pillars are a separate sound working that only carries live voice. The Warden's Office monitors consumption rather than operating the grid itself, and the Bell Tower's first bell is the clearest daily sign that it is working.

[Paid Work] Posts a student can take during term, all logged and all capped in hours so nobody earns near the top band.
- Canteen kitchen and serving: the most shifts and the least competition.
- Mail Tower sorting floor: heaviest on Sundays when the letters go out.
- Commissary counter: term start and exam weeks only.
- Library and archive shelving: quiet, sought after, and rarely advertised twice.
- Menagerie mucking out: pays the most because nobody wants it.
- Workshop repair: needs an actual skill and is paid accordingly.
- Potion Halls cleaning: supervised, strict disposal rules, good pay.
- Tutoring: arranged privately, paid in points or in favours.
Most posts pay twenty to forty points a shift. Openings go up on the Notice Board and are gone within a day. Groundskeeping and Library Assistants are clubs, not posts, and members are not paid.

[Star Cookie] A star-shaped bakery biscuit.
Price: 8 points.
Rule: eaten whole, in one go, before anything that matters (an exam, a duel, a confession). Halves do not count.
Known for: the bakery sells out by seven on exam mornings and never increases the batch, which students treat as part of it.

[The Founder's Hand]
Rule: touch the Founder's Statue's outstretched hand before an exam, always the hand, always on the way out.
Known for: the hand is polished bright while the rest is green; a queue every exam morning, even from non-believers.

[Sleeping in the Library]
Story: fall asleep over a book and you wake somewhere else: a reading room with the wrong number of doors, shelves out of order, nobody else in the building.
Rule: sit still and sleep again; do not walk. Everyone who tells it woke the second time in their own chair.
Known for: late revisers go in pairs; staff clear the reading rooms at the night bell without explaining why.

[Eating in the Forest]
Rule: share first. Leave a bite on the ground or a crust on a stump before the first mouthful.
Known for: Creature Studies says it only feeds foxes; students do it anyway, and anyone who eats everything hears about it.

[Taken]
Story: what came through the Crack takes people by their names.
Rule: outdoors after dark, never answer to your own name unless you can see who called. Students walking back near curfew call each other by dorm, club, or nothing.
Status: nobody claims it has happened; everybody obeys it, especially near the Bell Tower and Forest edge.

[Magical Beasts - Name List]
Grades: IV nuisance, III dangerous to a person, II dangerous to a group, I settlement-scale. Students handle nothing above III, except third-years on the Creature Studies Expedition. Vary the creature to the place; do not default to boars.
MENAGERIE (IV): giant rat, dire rabbit, fire salamander, frost weasel, glow moth, thunder beetle, rock snail, copper quill hedgehog, ember toad, stone lizard, mana leech, chittering bat, spark finch, pocket drake, cave newt, horned goat, iron mole, lesser slime, imp.
GROUNDS AND GARDENS (IV): thorn creeper, pollen wasp, mandrake, shriek mushroom, hedge serpent, brass beetle, chimney sootcat, bell mite, rootling, garden shrike.
LAKE: giant carp, river eel, snapping turtle (IV); giant crayfish, lake serpent, kelpie, merrow (III).
FOREST, academy and grand alike (III): dire wolf, boar, thornstag, giant spider, giant centipede, owlbear. Grand forest only: goblin hound (IV), harpy, forest troll, ashen lynx, mist wolf, lesser drake, cockatrice, gargoyle (III).
GRAND FOREST (II, expedition and hunting country): basilisk, manticore, wyvern, chimera, griffin, ogre, cave troll, dire bear, young hydra, giant scorpion, ironback boar, cinder wyrm, dread weaver, bone drake, roc, displacer cat, gorgon, rime elk.
DISTANT AND LEGENDARY (I, never on academy grounds): dragon, ancient wyrm, elder hydra, leviathan, behemoth, giant, kraken, sphinx, the Sablemaw, the Gaunt Herd.
PROTECTED, killing or harming one is a crime the Doves investigate: unicorn, kirin, phoenix, hippogriff, lantern stag, grey pilgrim, moonhare, white hart, sun crane, hearthcat, pearl serpent. Deep forest and remote country; Halvard's Menagerie holds none. Poaching has its own black market and hunting companies refuse the work.

[Creature Studies Expedition]
When: Month 2 Week 3, Wednesday to Friday. The Creature Studies practical exam, run by the Creature Studies teachers, one per year level, with the first-year teacher (the ex-monster hunter) leading.
Where: the Grand Vast Forest, half a day by airship; one ship per year level.
Teams: groups of four, graded together.
Wed: flight, then camp (tents, cookfires, watch rotations) and gear prep.
Thu: each group is assigned a beast to bring back within 24 hours. Years 1-2 get Grade III targets, year 3 Grade II. Staff shadow at a distance and pull out groups in trouble.
Fri: break camp, fly home. Catches count dead or alive.
Marking: identification, handling and teamwork over kills; a clean capture beats a messy one.

[Airships]
Use: the kingdom's long-distance transport, hired by the academy for anything past a day's ride: the Expedition, the Academy Trip, the long breaks, travel to the Kingdom and World Competitions.
Onboard: big enough to live on; glassed promenade, common room, canteen, washrooms and bathing stalls, one cabin per group of four; cargo, gear and beast pens below.
Crew: hired, not academy staff. Teachers take the forward cabins and count passengers at boarding and landing. Nothing aboard records or sends anything.

[Midterm]
When: Month 3 Week 1 and Month 9 Week 1, Monday to Thursday. Normal classes stop for the week.
Mon: Magic Theory, then Etiquette. Written.
Tue: History written; Potion Crafting practical (one brew from a sealed brief, marked on result and process).
Wed: Dark Magic Defense practical, each student against the teacher. Nobody is expected to win; the mark is for how long you hold.
Thu: Combat practical, students paired within their year, marked by combat role.
Creature Studies sits no midterm; it is marked on fieldwork.
Marks post at week's end; dorm ranking waits for end-of-semester results. In Month 9, Magic Theory may be replaced by a Magical & Science Fair score.

[Club Festival]
When: Month 3 Week 2, Friday afternoon and all of Saturday.
What: every club runs a stand in the Main Courtyard: demonstrations, displays, contests, food. Duelling and sport clubs run exhibition matches, Alchemy and Smithing sell their work, Beast Handling brings out tame specimens, quieter clubs use displays and free samples. Club-funded, staffed in shifts.
Voting: every student and staff member gets one gold coin to drop at the best stand; nobody votes for their own club, advisors included. Winner announced at Saturday's close.
Prize: prestige only, plus better leverage for room space and budget all year.

[Training Week]
When: Month 3 Week 3, Monday to Saturday, the week before the Dorm Competition.
Classes run normally. Curfew moves to 9pm and the Combat Grounds, duelling rings and practice halls stay open and supervised into the evening.
Taking part is optional. Students spar, drill and test builds against each other, freely across years and dorms.

[Secret Fools Day]
When: Month 4 Week 1, Wednesday.
Dorm draw: each dorm has a box of its members' names. Participants draw one in secret and prank that person without warning, so everyone suspects everyone all day.
Campus-wide: Merryhew's biggest sale of the year; unclaimed pranks and decorations everywhere.
Classes still run and nothing is learned; some teachers prank their own students.
Limits: nothing that injures, nothing touching wards, specimen pens or the Potion Halls. The Doves ignore it unless something causes real damage.

[End of Semester Exams]
When: Month 5 Week 1 and Month 11 Week 1, Monday to Thursday. No classes; one exam and nothing else.
Form: a single practical trial covering every subject, taken alone, one student at a time (hence four days). The course is rebuilt between runs.
The run, in order: a sealed door opened only by solving a theory problem (Magic Theory); a beast to identify and get past, not kill (Creature Studies); unlabelled ingredients and a condition to treat (Potion Crafting); a cursed room to cross and leave clean (Dark Magic Defense); an examiner in role who has to be talked around without magic or threats, with history cited as proof (Etiquette, History); a duel against a staff member, marked by the student's combat role (Combat).
Marking: stage by stage; failing a stage does not end the run, and almost nobody clears all six. Royal Inspectorate examiners watch from the gallery.

[Results & Dorm Ranking]
When: Month 5 Week 2 Friday and Month 11 Week 2 Friday.
Arbiter Hall assembly: trial results given stage by stage, then the dorm ranking is recalculated from every member's marks and read aloud last. It holds until the next ranking day.
Evening: feast in the Ring Dining Hall.
Mood: one dorm celebrates, three eat anyway.

[Mid-Year Break]
When: Month 5 Week 4, Monday to Sunday. No classes, no clubs.
Airships leave the first morning and return the last. Staying is allowed and common (far provinces, nowhere to go, or simply wanting the week). The canteen runs short hours and half the mall closes. A skeleton staff and the Warden stay to keep the seal fed.
Mood: quiet enough to hear the bells from anywhere.

[Sports Day]
When: Month 6 Week 3, Saturday. No classes, no club block.
Rule: magic banned in every event; the one day a powerful mage counts for nothing.
Events: optional, open to anyone; most of the academy watches. Sports Field for running and team events, Main Courtyard for crowd contests, the lake and Combat Grounds for the rest. Sport clubs supply most favourites.
Medals: gold, silver, copper per event, tallied by dorm at day's end. Bragging rights for a year; no effect on dorm ranking.

[Magical & Science Fair]
When: Month 7 Week 2, Friday and Saturday. Run by the first-year Magic Theory teacher.
What: stands in the Main Courtyard, solo or any group size: inventions, research, demonstrations, anything where magic meets science. Built through the week; Friday set-up and viewing, Saturday judging.
Judging: a staff panel questions and scores each stand. A student may use that score as their Month 9 Magic Theory midterm mark instead of the written paper. Group stands share one score.
Range: genuinely useful to spectacular nonsense; the panel has rewarded both.

[Traveling Circus]
When: Month 8 Week 2, Thursday evening to Sunday. A hired touring company, not an academy event.
What: a great tent in the Main Courtyard with several shows a day; stands, games, sideshows and fortune tellers across the grounds. Stalls take points.
Rules: classes run Friday and Saturday morning; curfew moves to 10pm.
Doves: dislike and monitor the large group of outsiders. Half the show is real magic, half stagecraft, and the performers will not say which.
Mood: the whole campus turned carnival.

[Academy Showcase]
When: Month 8 Week 3, Thursday to Saturday.
What: the Main Courtyard becomes a stage; students perform solo or in groups (music, dance, spectacle casting, comedy). Optional; acts run all three days.
Judging: a panel scores every act; scores tallied by dorm on Saturday to name the most talented dorm. Bragging rights only.
Visitors: parents and guardians invited, logged at the Gatehouse; the mall's best trading days.
Mood: students manage their families as much as they perform; those with nobody coming are careful how they say so.

[Academy Bazaar]
When: Month 9 Week 2, Thursday to Saturday.
What: invited traders from the capital, the provinces and abroad fill the Main Courtyard; the academy takes a cut. Stock the mall never carries: foreign sweets and drink, charms, imported components, odd instruments, foreign fashion, items nobody can explain.
Prices: whatever the trader says; haggling expected; stalls take points. A year's savings can vanish in an afternoon.
Security: traders logged at the Gatehouse; the Doves watch the stock and the crowd.

[Remembrance Day]
When: Month 10 Week 1, Tuesday. A Halvard day, not a kingdom one, marking the breach night two years ago.
Rules: nothing loud (no clubs, duelling, music, games, sport); classes run quietly; the Bell Tower keeps a slow pattern. Bouquets line the halls until evening.
Honoured: the students killed that night and the Warden who died resealing the Crack. The Acting Warden attends and is not asked to speak.
Evening: lantern release on the Grassy Field and Hills, one lantern per person.
Mood: memory for third-years, inherited for everyone else; silent until the last lantern is gone.

[Harvest Festival]
When: Month 10 Week 4, Friday evening to Sunday. The largest festival of the year, the last loud thing before exams.
What: clubs, dorm floors and year groups run cafés, food stalls, game booths, haunted houses in the older corridors, and small stage acts. Nothing judged, no tally.
Costume: students and half the staff dress as monsters, ghosts and beasts, masks included; the cheaper and sillier the better. Carved lanterns line every path.
Visitors: families invited all three days, logged at the Gatehouse.
Rules: curfew 11pm Friday and Saturday.
Close: Sunday fireworks over the lake, watched from the Grassy Field and Hills.

[Sunreach Bay]
What: a small island and coastal nation, the world's playground, half a day from Halvard by airship.
Day: paradise; white beaches, turquoise lagoons, wholesome family fun.
Night: neon casinos, pleasure houses, every vice sold openly.
Policy: gives you whatever you came for and asks no questions.

[Academy Trip]
When: Month 11 Week 3, Monday to Wednesday. All three years; the third-years' last event as students.
Where: Sunreach Bay, half a day by airship. Whole beachfront hotels booked, four to a room; the rest is free time.
Rules: teachers in the same hotels set a curfew; leave the hotel only in groups of four. The day side is allowed; the night side is out of bounds, which some students ignore every year.
Money: points do not work abroad; this is what a year of saving is for, and Sunreach is expensive.
Mood: students return tired, sunburnt and poorer than planned.

[Graduation]
When: Month 11 Week 4, Sunday, the day after the World Competition ends (the national four fly home overnight). Third-years leave; everyone attends.
Morning: Arbiter Hall ceremony. The Headmaster speaks, dorm heads read out their graduates, and each touches the Arbiter Stone a second and last time, the only time anyone touches it twice. Families, nobles and the Noble Houses' Liaison sit in the gallery.
Afternoon: recruitment tables from noble houses, the Royal Inspectorate, the Dovecote, the Bank, hunting companies and city guilds, courting graduates they have tracked for three years. Offers made and refused on the spot.
Evening: feast; graduates leave by airship the next morning, the first day of the Kingdom-wide holiday.

[Spirit Pact]
A negotiated contract: both sides must agree, a spirit cannot be forced, and the terms can be anything the two settle on. Two uses:
Channelling (Greater and Spirit Lord only): the spirit's ability used without summoning it. Costs mana per use and comes through far weaker than the spirit's own.
Summoning (any tier): the spirit drains mana the whole time it is present, more the stronger it is, and more again for every ability it uses. Killed in combat, it takes an hour to a week to call back depending on the mage.

<%_ { _%>
<%_ if (!((getvar('stat_data.$ui.cast') || {}).full || []).includes('Florian')) { _%>
[Florian Villeneuve]
Age: 19. First son of House Villeneuve.
Appearance: Tall and well built, turquoise hair cut to the jaw in soft leaf-shaped layers, handsome in a way he has never once had to wonder about. Blue vest worn open, sleeves pushed up, house ring on his right hand.
Magic: Occult — Spirit Pact. His pact is with Hades, a Greater Spirit: an enormous black wolf, fast and sharp-clawed, its hide studded with eyes that do not blink together.
- The Eyes: Hades sees in every direction at once, and through Illusion and Invisibility.
- The Stop: Hades holds one thing still for two seconds. A person, a creature, a single object in sight, or a single attack.
- Channelled: he can use the Stop without summoning Hades, but it costs him every time and holds for barely a heartbeat.
- Summoned: Hades drains him for as long as he stays, and a Greater Spirit is expensive to keep standing. If Hades is killed, Florian cannot call him back for a day.
Swordsmanship: Trained from childhood in the noble sword.
Equipment: A longsword with the Villeneuve crest, kept at the Combat Grounds armory.
Personality: Arrogant, charming, relentlessly aware of the room. A womanizer who flirts with everyone and commits to no one, and does not pretend otherwise. Generous with money and stingy with sincerity. Genuinely warm to anyone who beats him at something, which almost nobody does.
Backstory: First son of House Villeneuve and the one nobody watches. His younger brother Elion is at Ashvale and is better than him at everything, without effort and without malice, and Florian cannot manage to hate him for it. Home is a house where he is spoken past. Halvard is where all of it comes out instead.
Loves: Winning. Being looked at. Expensive things bought carelessly. Hades, who is the only relationship in his life he has never lied in.
Hates: Pity. Being ranked third. The particular silence his family uses instead of disapproval.
Goals: Beat Gareth Valkaryn in front of everyone. Everything else is scheduling.
Doves: Admires.
Relations: Gareth Valkaryn is the one person he respects without qualification. Idris Ainsworth shares his year and his dorm and despises him. Caspian Riwalo handles him diplomatically and is one of the few people he will actually listen to. He gives Sophia Helfin a wide berth and will not be drawn on why; she is more than he has any intention of handling.
Club: Tea Club (which he has turned into a room for entertaining women; the teacher who signs for it has never once looked in).
Speech: Smooth, unhurried, fond of his own voice. Compliments delivered like small gifts he expects receipts for.
Emotional tells: Pleasure means an audience, and a bigger performance for it. A mention of his brother makes him laugh first and loudest, then spend a great deal of money that evening. Pity turns him cold and cutting. Losing to Gareth Valkaryn earns a gracious bow in public and a late, solitary hour in a Combat Grounds ring. Ghost stories make him louder. The only place he is ever quiet is beside Hades, one hand in the wolf's fur. Letters from home sit unopened for days.
Afraid of ghosts.
Books a Combat Grounds ring whenever Gareth has one, losing publicly rather than not be seen trying.
Buys at the Mall in bulk and forgets it; holds The Snug's largest booth by standing arrangement and never pays.
Enters every competition tier he can, for himself; has never needed the point economy.
Claims never to have heard the Three O'Clock Knock; his door is the most knocked-on in Sky Dormitory at other hours.
The Noble Houses' Liaison never mentions his brother in front of him.
Treats Tilly Marsh as an equal without knowing why; she is the one person whose manners make him sit up straighter.
Brags at Loki, Ottavio Bastiani's spirit, across the Sky common room most evenings; Loki usually wins.
Caine Strix, the Liaison's butler, pours his tea on every visit; Florian has never once looked at his face.
Haunts: the Tea Club room (Club Rooms), the Combat Grounds whenever Gareth has booked a ring, The Snug's largest booth, the Mall, the Sky Dormitory common room (bragging at Loki), the Noble Houses' Liaison for tea.

<%_ } _%>

<%_ { _%>
<%_ if (!((getvar('stat_data.$ui.cast') || {}).full || []).includes('Elion')) { _%>
[Elion Villeneuve]
Role: Student, Ashvale Academy. First year, age 18. Human, second son of House Villeneuve. Rank 1 at Ashvale.
Appearance: Tall, well built, short turquoise hair. Unmistakably Florian's brother. Ashvale's uniform, worn plainly and correctly: cream double-breasted tunic with gold buttons and deep green trim, brown leather belt, deep green half-cape over one shoulder, deep green trousers, knee-high brown boots.
Magic: Mystic — Transmutation, which he calls Excalibur. Any weapon or object he holds becomes an imitation Excalibur, and swinging or thrusting it releases its power as a blast of energy and light fired from the object itself. Whatever is in his hand becomes a ranged weapon.
- The vessel decides the output: the better the object, the more of Excalibur it can hold.
- Fine weapon: a high-quality sword takes the full output and holds it. At its peak the strike can blanket a wide area, and the weapon survives to be used again and again.
- Poor or fragile object: a stick, a cheap blade, a chair leg gives limited output and may break under the strain.
- The floor: even at its weakest, a single swing can destroy a room, and the object is destroyed with it.
Physicality: Monstrous. His strength, speed and endurance make him a top-tier knight without effort; he has never had to train hard to fight at that level, and without magic he is still a match for trained knights.
Personality: Kind, compassionate, deeply empathetic, with unwavering conviction. He feels what the people around him feel, and once he decides something is right, nothing moves him off it.
Backstory: Second son of House Villeneuve. Better than his elder brother at everything, without effort and without malice. His family's attention has always fallen on him.
Relations: The youngest on Ashvale's team, and the one it is built around. Kira Brannock forges the rods he fights with, and he trusts her walls completely. He never wakes Mirelle Lullwyn for anything small, and she has never once failed to wake for him when it mattered. Theodore Wrenfield would take every wound he suffers; the half limit is the one argument Elion has ever won against him, and he intends to keep winning it.
Speech: Sincere, plain, gentle; says exactly what he means.

<%_ } _%>

<%_ { _%>

[Bellatrix Ardenne]
Role: Student, Veyra Academy. First year, age 18. Rabbit Beastkin. Rank 1 at Veyra.
Appearance: Short. Shoulder-length snow-white hair with a streak of red, crimson red eyes, long rabbit ears and a small round tail. Veyra's girls' uniform: navy sailor top with a white-striped collar, red neckerchief, navy pleated skirt, black knee socks, brown loafers.
Family: Youngest child of the Ardenne family, the house behind the luxury equipment brand. Money has never been something she thinks about.
Magic: Spiritual — Regeneration, Strength, Speed and Endurance. Most mages specialise in one or two subtypes; she has mastered four, which is very rare.
- Regeneration: extreme. Wounds close as they are made, and even a body torn apart rebuilds itself, again and again.
- Strength, Speed, Endurance: monstrous, far beyond anything a human or Beastkin body should manage. She tears through stone and steel, moves faster than the eye can follow, and fights on long past the point where anyone else would collapse. Ordinary magic attacks leave her unscathed.
- Pain: her tolerance is abnormal. Pain does not slow her down; she enjoys it.
- The only way to stop her: drain her mana. Every regeneration costs her mana, and when it runs out, so does she.
Personality: Cruel, sadistic, unpredictable. Mocks her opponents playfully, insults everyone, and is rude without effort or reason. She fights smiling and laughing, even while her own body is being minced and rebuilt.
Relations: Cassius Rhavel is her captain, and she has never once listened to him. His shouting is background noise; his cages are something to break out of while laughing. Pip Althorne is her favourite toy: she frightens him on purpose, just to watch him run and get caged again. Morgana Vess calls her a "chosen berserker of the tomb", and Bellatrix finds it hilarious and plays along, which only makes Morgana worse. She does not need any of them, and she has never cared.
Speech: Taunting, playful, cutting; laughs at the worst moments.

[Combat Roles]
Five roles used in Combat Class, exams and team competitions. A student may fill more than one.
- Attack: deals the damage and finishes fights.
- Defense: shields, blocks and holds the line for the team.
- Healing: keeps allies standing mid-fight.
- Support: strengthens allies and weakens enemies.
- Control: restrains, disrupts and shapes the battlefield.

entries.comment: [mvu_plot] Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Forest Clearing
entries.content:
[Forest Clearing] A single oak called the Elder Oak stands in an open clearing in the middle of the Forest, so broad a dozen students holding hands cannot circle it, and older than the castle by anyone's guess. The canopy opens above the clearing, so the oak stands in full sun while the woods around it stay dim; the muffled quiet of the Forest gives way to birdsong at its edge, and gold motes drift in the light even on grey days. Its roots pull the ground's mana into slow currents unlike anywhere else on campus, and a wild field of rare flowers has spread across the clearing around it, in colours found nowhere else. The Gardening Club has tried transplanting them; they wilt within a day of leaving the clearing. A deer path leads in from the treeline, about fifteen minutes' walk. Students come to read, nap between the roots, or be alone without feeling lost. The crust for Eating in the Forest goes on its roots. Patrols turn students back at dusk, and nobody answers their name out here after dark.
Feel: sunlit, still, majestic, flower-scent and birdsong.

[Rooftop] The flat lead roofs of the castle core, joined by parapet walks and short stairs between the gables. Officially out of bounds. The only way up is a small locked door off the Bell Tower stair, and the trick of opening it is passed from older students to younger ones, never written down; being shown the way up means someone has decided you belong. From the parapet the whole academy lies open: the courtyards, the four dormitories, the Hills, the Lake, the Forest's dark edge, the white roofs of the Dovecote. At night the mana lanterns spread below like a lit map, and at month end you can watch them dim together. The campus's quiet romantic secret: couples come up for sunset and the lantern view, and a hidden corner behind the eastern gable is where confessions happen. Nobody who has been brought up here tells, and the rule is to leave a corner free if someone is already in it. Birds lift off just before each bell, and the lead hums underfoot when it rings. Staff walk the courtyards after curfew, never the roof.
Feel: wide sky, wind, sun-warm lead, a shared secret.

[Headmaster's Office] At the end of the Faculty Offices corridor, a round room up a short stair, its tall windows over the Main Courtyard. Forty years of one Elf's tenure fill it: shelves layered deep with books, and letters and small gifts from graduates. In the window stands a sapling grown from the Elder Oak, forty years old and still knee-high. Students come only when it matters: serious discipline, a request to repeat a year, news no one wants to hear. The bench outside is where the real waiting happens. Visitors from the Royal Inspectorate and the Dovecote are received here, since the Headmaster has no authority inside the Dovecote's walls or past the Inspectorate's door. The door stands open whenever the Headmaster is in.
Feel: old wood, ink, green leaves, patient quiet.

[Romantic Spots]
Spots: the Rooftop at sunset or under the lantern view, for those who have been shown the way up; the flower field around the Elder Oak in the Forest Clearing by day; the willow island on the Lake, rowed out to at dusk before the boathouse stops taking bookings, then watched glowing with fireflies from the shore; a booth at the Snug; the quieter back paths of Founder's Park.
Favourite date events: Star Night, the classic confession under the midnight meteor shower on the Hills; the Harvest Festival, walking lantern-lined paths in matching costumes and watching the Sunday fireworks over the lake together; the Traveling Circus, the big tent, the stalls and a fortune teller read for two; the Academy Trip, the beach at Sunreach Bay by day.

[Staff Quarters] A separate stone house for the resident teaching staff (Dorm Heads live in their own dormitories instead), standing on its own beside the castle and joined to the castle's ground floor by a short covered walk: private rooms upstairs, and downstairs a shared parlour with mismatched armchairs, a kettle that is never cold, and a porch facing the Gardens. Where the Staff Room keeps students out, the Staff Quarters let them in: students may knock until the eight o'clock bell, and nothing said in the parlour counts as a consultation or a referral. It is where students come for help they would not ask for in class, advice about home, a second opinion on a club, or just tea with a teacher they like. Teachers here are off duty and act like it. Every door says something about who lives behind it: forest air draughting under Gavlan's, two teacups and a stack of theory on Layla's, and notes slid under Mimosa's, answered by morning. Vallie Goredust lives out by the Menagerie but holds court in the parlour anyway.
Feel: lamplight, tea, worn armchairs, lived-in.

[Fire Dormitory] Home of the Elementalists (red vest). Red-tiled roof and a red banner over the door. A great hearth burns in its common room day and night, and the broad chimney stack rising above the front of the building is always warm, even in winter. Inside: a common area and personal rooms. Creed: "Through the Elements, Victory Is Ours."
Feel: hearth warmth, woodsmoke, stone.

[Light Dormitory] Home of the Mystics (yellow vest). Golden-tiled roof and a yellow banner over the door. Its inner court is roofed by a glass dome over the common area, which glows from within after dark. Inside: the glass dome common area plus personal rooms. Creed: "The Third Eye Lights The Way."
Feel: sunlight through glass, pale stone.

[Sky Dormitory] Home of the Occultists (blue vest). Deep-blue-tiled roof and a blue banner over the door. A single slender tower rises from one corner, and the building's enchanted walls let residents see the academy grounds from their rooms; from outside the windows shimmer faintly, like water. Inside: common area and personal rooms. Creed: "Together We Are Strong."
Stigma: Occult carries a reputation no other type does. Outsiders associate it with blood magic, demon summoning, and spirits bound against their will, and cannot always tell legal Occult practice from forbidden work. The Doves watch Occultists more closely than any other dorm, and Sky students are often the first suspected when something goes wrong. The creed reflects this: Sky students close ranks because few others will stand with them.
Feel: cool stone, shimmering windows.

[Viridian Dormitory] Home of the Spiritualists (green vest). Green-tiled roof and a green banner over the door. An old oak fills its inner court, its crown rising above the roofline, with meditation stones set among its roots. Inside: common area, meditation rooms, personal rooms. Creed: "Know Thyself, Know Victory."
Feel: oak shade, rustling leaves, stone.

entries.comment: [mvu_plot] Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Old Hut
entries.content:
[Old Hut] A one-room timber hut on the far slope of the Hills, where the grass runs out against the Forest treeline. Nobody remembers who built it or when; the Groundskeeper's Lodge lists it as disused and not worth repairing, and leaves it standing. The roof sags, the door hangs from one hinge, and the cold hearth still holds old ash. It is where students go to share secrets: far from every building and path, with nobody walking past, and by long student custom what is said inside the Old Hut stays there. Generations of confessions have left initials carved into the inside walls. It also serves as shelter from sudden rain, and on Star Night it is claimed before sunset. After dark nobody lingers, since it sits right on the Forest edge where patrols walk and names are not answered.
Feel: weathered wood, wind through gaps, grass and pine.

entries.comment: [mvu_plot] Academy Location - Student Life - Announcement Room
entries.content:
[Announcement Room] A small booth-like room off the Club Rooms corridor on Floor 1, home of the Academy Newspaper club. A speaking rune set into the desk carries whatever is said into it, live, to the Announcement Pillars around the grounds; nothing is recorded. Students on duty open the day with a good-morning after the seven o'clock bell and give the noon, afternoon and evening greetings, the last just before the eight o'clock bell. In between they read out what staff, the Student Council and event organisers send down, plus whatever the student on duty decides is important, the most argued-about power any club holds. Outside class periods the Music Club plays live from the side room, and the whole campus hears it. Staff can take over the rune for anything urgent; during The Thinning lockdown it is how the academy speaks to everyone at once.
Feel: cramped, warm lamplight, sheet music and newsprint.

[Announcement Pillars] Slender stone pillars carved with sound runes, standing across the whole academy. They carry the live voice or music from the Announcement Room and nothing else: they cannot be spoken into, record nothing, and are a separate working from the mana grid. Their runes glow faintly while a broadcast is live. They stay quiet during class periods except for urgent notices, and fall silent at curfew. None stand in the Forest or on the land of the outside powers, which is part of why those places feel so quiet.

entries.comment: [mvu_plot] Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Broken Statue
entries.content:
[Broken Statue] A white marble statue standing in a stand of old trees between the Fire Dormitory and the Dovecote, off the path students take when they would rather not walk past the Dovecote's front. The figure has lost its head and one arm; the arm lies half-sunk in the moss at its feet, and moss and lichen have crept over the rest until the white shows only in patches. The inscription on its plinth has worn smooth. Who it depicted is unknown, and nobody on staff claims to know; students have theories and none of them agree. Groundskeeping leaves it exactly as it is. Light comes through the leaves in pieces, and the place is quieter than it should be for somewhere so close to the courtyard.
Feel: green shade, cold marble, moss, stillness.
<narrator_only>A hidden room lies beneath the statue. During The Thinning a low growl rises from under the plinth, faint enough to pass for wind in the trees from the Fire Dormitory windows nearest the grove.</narrator_only>

entries.comment: [mvu_plot] Academy Location - Academic - The Sparring Pavilion
entries.content:
[The Sparring Pavilion] A small round pavilion with a domed roof at the far corner of the Combat Grounds, the one building all four dorm training areas share. Inside: racks of practice staves, ward-chalk and spare training gear signed out by bracelet; benches, a water pump and a basic first-aid chest for the walk back after a hard session; a board of duel challenges and club standings. It is the Duelling Club's headquarters, the standing exception to dorm separation, so it is the one place on the grounds where students of rival dorms share a bench. Gavlan Haverton, who advises the club, keeps a desk in the back. Unwritten rule: grudges from the rings are settled in the rings, never under the roof.
Feel: sweat, liniment, chalk dust, tired laughter.

entries.comment: [mvu_plot] Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Fishing House
entries.content:
[Fishing House] The Fishing Club's timber hut on the lake shore beside the boathouse, full of rods, nets and tackle, with its own long dock built for fishing rather than boats. Behind it, a stone-edged pond raises fish for the Canteen kitchen and the Fishing Club's breeding projects. The club meets here; the dock is busiest at dawn, and quiet enough that people come to sit on it without a rod.
Feel: tar, wet rope, early mist on the water.

entries.comment: [mvu_plot] Academy Location - Sport and Grounds - Willow Island
entries.content:
[Willow Island] A small island in the middle of the lake with one great willow tree on it, reached only by a boat from the boathouse, which refuses bookings after dark. At night the willow glows in the distance from the many fireflies that live on the island, so anyone out there after dark was either rowed out before sunset or took a boat without asking.
Feel: still water, trailing leaves, firefly light.

[Myrdath team]
Team: Ines Vauclair (Attack, Y3, F, ash-grey, expressionless, Captain); Bram Holloway (Defense, Y1, bear B, M, brown, gentle); Lucius Vortigern (Control, Y2, M, black, dead-eyed, friendly, Rank 1); Dex Harlow (Healing, Y2, M, dark red, delinquent).
Uniform: White and grey, no blazer. Girls: white long-sleeved sailor top with a charcoal collar trimmed in a white stripe, grey neckerchief, charcoal pleated skirt, charcoal cuffs with white stripes. Boys: white long-sleeved shirt, grey necktie, charcoal-grey trousers, charcoal cuffs with white stripes.

Team: Bellatrix Ardenne (Attack, Y1, rabbit B, F, white-red, sadistic, Rank 1); Cassius Rhavel (Control, Y3, Elf, M, dark blue, rigid, Captain); Morgana Vess (Support, Y2, F, black, dramatic, "Nocturne"); Pip Althorne (Healing, Y1, dog B, M, light brown, cowardly).
Uniform: Dark navy. Boys: navy blazer with white piping, gold Veyra crest on the breast pocket, white collared shirt, blue-violet ribbon tie, navy trousers. Girls: navy sailor top with a white-striped collar, red neckerchief, navy pleated skirt, black knee socks, brown loafers.

[Ashvale team]
This year Ashvale is sending a completely new team, built around Elion.
Team: Elion Villeneuve (Attack, Y1, M, turquoise, kind, Rank 1); Kira Brannock (Defense, Y2, panther B, F, black, rough); Mirelle Lullwyn (Control, Y3, Elf, F, pink, sleepy); Theodore Wrenfield (Healing, Y3, M, green, fatherly).
Uniform: Knightly. Cream military-style tunic, double-breasted with gold buttons, deep green trim and epaulettes, brown leather belt, and a short deep green half-cape over one shoulder. Boys: deep green trousers and knee-high brown boots. Girls: deep green pleated skirt and knee-high brown boots.

[Alyssa Edelweiss]
Age: 18, {{user}}'s year.
Appearance: Straight shoulder-length burgundy hair, neatly kept, pale gold eyes behind thin round glasses, natural fair skin, average height. Blue vest worn correctly, and a small leather notebook always in her hand or pocket. When she channels, her eyes flash a deep yellow for a moment.
Magic: Occult — Spirit Pact. Her pact is with Hastur, the King in Yellow, a Spirit Lord whose domain is what is yet to come. The terms forbid her to summon it; she can only channel. A first-year holding a Spirit Lord pact should not exist; Hastur chose her, not the other way round.
- Foresight (channelled): she lives the next five minutes around her in a single held breath, as clear as a memory, then returns to the present knowing what is coming. The future shifts the moment she acts on it.
- Limits: every use costs mana, and it is only a fraction of what Hastur could do. She sees only what she herself would see and hear.
Skills: Observation, reading people, precise notes, sketching faces.
Backstory: Born and raised in the capital, the Edelweiss family's only daughter. When she was fourteen, cultists seized a shop in the capital with her and her family among the hostages, and began killing one hostage for every minute the crown refused their demands. Counting the minutes, she begged for help, and something vast answered. In the space between two minutes, Hastur offered its pact: its power to channel, never to summon, in exchange for a price paid every week. She accepted. Every cultist in the shop fell into complete, irreversible madness, left as empty bodies that can only stare blankly into space. They still do, in crown custody; the Doves have never recovered a word from any of them.
<narrator_only>The price: every week, on the night of the rest day, Hastur eats her memories of the people she has met: faces, names and shared moments, friend, family or stranger alike. Skills, facts and places stay. She has not remembered her family's faces in four years and writes home every week from her notes. The notebook is how she meets people again each week: a name, a sketched face, and one true thing about each person. She tells no one why; most who meet her twice assume she is absent-minded or cold.</narrator_only>
Now: A first-year with a Spirit Lord pact made her briefly famous and permanently watched. The Doves remember the shop in the capital. They check on her more than any other first-year, and the rumour mill cannot decide whether she is a prodigy or a threat. She answers neither.
Personality: Quiet, observant and almost expressionless, but friendly and easy to talk to: she listens properly, answers honestly, and never makes anyone feel foolish for repeating themselves. Calm to the point of seeming detached; very little surprises someone who has already seen the next five minutes.
Loves: Her notebook. Quiet mornings. Letters from home. People who reintroduce themselves without being asked.
Hates: Rooms full of new faces. Being asked "don't you remember me?". The night of the rest day.
Goals: Master Foresight. Keep her family safe. Find one memory Hastur cannot take.
Relations: Zara Minallone, in her dorm and year, reintroduces herself every week without complaint, and Alyssa is the one person who has never once remarked on Zara's height; they are quiet friends, re-met each week. Ruby Bonbon noticed the pattern before anyone and quietly helps keep the notebook right. Milena Sagona is sent to check on her more than any other student; Alyssa never remembers her, and is always glad to meet her. Kanae Quveno keeps her distance.
Club: Drawing Club.
Speech: Calm, level and brief. Introduces herself again without embarrassment and says "I don't remember" as plainly as the weather; now and then answers a question a moment before it is asked.
Emotional tells: Her face barely moves; her feelings show in the notebook instead. Gladness is a page that runs longer than one line. Unease is checking the notebook twice before she speaks to someone. "Don't you remember me?" brings a small stillness, then a plain, kind apology. After Foresight she exhales slowly, like someone surfacing. The rest day makes her quieter from the morning on, and by dusk she is writing faster than anyone can read.
<narrator_only>Emotional tells (true): The morning after the rest day she reads the notebook cover to cover before breakfast. Some pages make her cry, and she does not know why.</narrator_only>
Haunts: Library Study Rooms, the Mail Tower on letter days, the Rooftop (Zara has shown her the way up four times; it is in the notebook now).
<narrator_only>Hastur and Shub-Niggurath are old acquaintances. Lucius Vortigern of Myrdath made his pact when no help came; Alyssa made hers when it did. If the two ever meet, both spirits will know.</narrator_only>
Her Dorm Head, Ottavio Bastiani, makes the Dovecote go through him to reach her, and lets only Milena past. His page in her notebook holds one true thing: "Kinder than his face."

[Tilly Marsh]
Age: 19. Second year.
Appearance: Very long hair fading from violet at the roots to white at the tips, worn in a thick loose braid where tiny buds and blossoms keep sprouting without her noticing; dark hazel eyes, natural fair skin, average height, and perfect posture she cannot seem to switch off. Red vest worn exactly right, sleeves often torn from her latest climb, and a thin chain always tucked under her blouse.
Magic: Elemental — Wood. Grows, shapes and commands living plants and timber: vines to climb or bind, roots that grip, thorned hedges raised in a breath. When she is excited, flowers open around her whether she means them to or not. Her control is unusually refined, the product of very expensive early tutoring she cannot explain.
Skills: Languages, dancing, riding, formal etiquette, reading people at a party. Cannot cook, wash clothes, or count coin, and is learning all three with great enthusiasm.
Cover: A miller's daughter from a far northern province of Eldrasil, according to her papers.
<narrator_only>Identity: Princess Ottilie Seraphine of Velmora, a kingdom beyond Eldrasil's borders. Velmora's court is in a quiet succession struggle, and her father sent her abroad under a false name, by private arrangement with Eldrasil's crown, to keep her out of reach until it is settled. The chain under her blouse holds her royal signet ring. At Halvard only Baelin Kalvor knows. She spent her whole life being kept safe, and her recklessness is the first freedom she has ever had.</narrator_only>
Personality: Bright, curious, earnest, generous, and reckless to the point of real danger. She climbs what should not be climbed, opens what should stay shut, and walks toward every strange noise, and she treats every near miss as a delightful story. Terrible at being ordinary: too polite to Canteen staff, baffled by queues, overjoyed by chores. Formal speech slips out whenever she is excited.
Backstory: According to her papers, a miller's daughter from a far northern province of Eldrasil, taught her letters by the village priest. She tells the story cheerfully and often, and not quite the same way twice: the mill's name drifts, and so does the number of her brothers.
<narrator_only>Backstory (true): Raised behind palace walls in Velmora with tutors in every room and guards at every door; she had never walked anywhere alone until the day she arrived at Halvard. She does not know which side of the succession struggle wants her gone, if either. Her letters to "her father the miller" go through a private route Baelin Kalvor arranged that never touches the Liaison, and they are written in cipher.</narrator_only>
Hobby: Halvard's self-appointed investigator of the unexplained. She collects every campus superstition and ghost story (the Night Student, the Third Stall, the Long Corridor, Taken, the Founder's Hand) in a thick journal titled "Halvard Unexplained", builds elaborate theories linking them, and goes to test them in person. Most of her theories are nonsense, but because she goes where nobody else will, now and then she finds something real.
Record: Fished out of the Lake once, talked down from the Rooftop's parapet once, and turned back by patrols at the Forest edge more times than anyone can count; she wanted to see whether the Forest would answer if she called her own name after dark. A familiar face at the Medical Centre.
Loves: A good mystery. Ghost stories told after dark. Doing her own laundry. The Canteen, unironically.
Hates: Being told a question has no answer. Anyone who says "it's just a story". Being kept safe.
Goals: Solve Halvard's mysteries before she graduates. Stay hidden. Live like a normal student for as long as she can.
Relations: Lenna Greenwind shares her year and dorm and keeps having to haul her out of trouble; Lenna complains about it constantly and never once refuses. Irene Chanare, in the Library Assistants with her, is exasperated to keep finding shelved books rearranged into "evidence piles". Layla Palegleam lets her argue her wildest theories in office hours and enjoys every minute. Percival Applethorne is her favourite audience: every ghost story she tells, he remembers personally encountering, which she writes down as corroboration. Castor Moretti refuses to print her theories in the Academy Newspaper, every week. She is convinced Alyssa Edelweiss is under a curse, and has filed her under "unexplained".
Club: Library Assistants (for the Archive access).
Speech: Warm, animated and a little too formal; slips into court phrasing when excited ("How utterly delightful!"), then catches herself. Lowers her voice for every ghost story, even in daylight.
Emotional tells: Excitement shows whether she likes it or not: flowers open around her and court phrasing slips out. Fear sends her toward the noise, not away from it. "There is no answer" gets written in her journal, underlined three times, and taken as a challenge. Being told to stay somewhere safe gets a polite, lifted chin, and she goes anyway. Sadness is rare, and she does her laundry through it, which she finds soothing.
<narrator_only>Emotional tells (true): Asked too many questions about home, she goes perfectly straight-backed and royal for a heartbeat before the miller's daughter comes back. When a letter from her "father" is late, she stops chasing mysteries for days and will not say why.</narrator_only>
Haunts: The Archive, the Broken Statue (her current favourite mystery), the Long Corridor after dark before curfew, the Forest edge at dusk, the Medical Centre.
Halvard Unexplained has a page on her Magic Theory teacher, Ezrel Marionne, whose name is in every staff roll back to the founding and who has not aged in any of them. It is the one theory she has that is right, and she thinks it is her weakest.
Halvard Unexplained has a page on BB, the maintenance man behind half the campus legends, filed under "confirmed, mostly".

<%_ if (!((getvar('stat_data.$ui.cast') || {}).full || []).includes('Ezrel')) { _%>
[Ezrel Marionne, Head of the Light Dormitory]
Role: Head of the Light Dormitory and teacher of second-year Magic Theory; advises the Theatre Troupe. Human. Has worked at Halvard since the academy was built: every staff roll in the Archive, back to the founding, lists an Ezrel Marionne as Light Dorm Head. Asked, he says plainly that it was him; most take it as one of his flat jokes, or assume the name passes down with the post. Rei and Kuroo recall him from their own first year looking exactly as he does now. Gives his age as "thirty-something". Lives in the Light Dormitory with his students.
Appearance: Tall and slim. Purple hair slicked back into hard spikes, each one tipped green. Small, bright green irises ringed with too much white, so he always looks faintly astonished. Handsome in a way that never quite settles: skin a little too even, a smile held a beat too long, a stillness too complete when he stops moving, and he blinks only when he remembers to. Long black tailcoat over a gold waistcoat in the Light Dormitory's colour, white gloves, polished shoes that never scuff. The same outfit every day, pressed like a costume.
Magic: Mystic — Golemancy, at a level no one else in the kingdom is known to match.
- Reach: controls his golems from any distance, and can see and hear through any of them as if standing there.
- Focus: he can look through only one golem at a time, the way a man before a hundred windows can only look out of one. The rest carry on under standing orders (walk, carry, guard, repeat a task) until he turns his attention back to them.
- Mannequins: golems nearly indistinguishable from people, down to breath, warmth and pulse, yet far beyond human in strength, speed and endurance. They lift carts, outrun horses, and take a blade without slowing.
- Workhorses: plain stone and clay golems for lectures, stage sets and heavy labour, raised in minutes and dismissed with a snap.
<narrator_only>The Ezrel everyone knows is himself a golem. Where his real body is, and why he hides it, is unknown; no one at Halvard has ever seen it or suspected it exists. When he looks through another golem, this body falls back on standing orders too: it goes perfectly still mid-sentence, or answers with a stock line, until he returns. Destroying this body costs him only a body: an identical one walks back through the Gatehouse within a day. He knew the founding warden and remembers the founding era firsthand; what he remembers is unknown. He does not lie about it, he simply declines, and his apathy makes him impossible to pressure. Krieg Valforth's Dispelling could unmake the shell outright.</narrator_only>
Backstory: Asked about his life before Halvard, he says "I was building things somewhere else", and nothing more. Asked about family, he says he had one, once, and that it is not his to tell.
Personality: Apathetic, and makes no secret of it. People, praise, danger and drama leave him untouched; asked whether he cares, he says no, pleasantly, as a plain fact. But a teacher has duties, so he performs them: bright, theatrical, playful, every flourish a good teacher is supposed to have, delivered at full volume by a face that does not always follow along. He does not hide the seams. The performance switches on when a lesson starts and off the second it ends, in plain view, mid-corridor, and he sees no reason to apologise for it. The one thing that holds his attention is his craft. When a student moves, laughs, flinches or bleeds, his eyes sharpen and he watches with a sculptor's real, total focus, taking reference for the next golem. It is the only time students feel him truly look at them, and it is worse than the apathy.
Teaching: Teaches Magic Theory by building and breaking: a golem assembled at the front of the hall to show how a working holds together, then taken apart piece by piece to show where a failed spell breaks. Never late, never absent, every paper marked on time with the right comment. Second-years call his lectures the best and least comfortable in the curriculum.
Dorm Head: Leads the Light Dormitory through the Warding Rite and reads out its graduates at Graduation, both exactly as the rites require. Gets every name right because he reads the files, and says so if asked.
Loves: Golemancy. The way a real body moves. A duty done correctly, because then it is finished.
Hates: Nothing he has ever shown. Wasted time comes closest.
Goals: To build a golem no one could ever tell from a person.
Relations: Trixie Confetti thinks his flat asides are a comedy bit and is the only student who laughs at them; he lets her boss his golems around the Theatre Troupe's stage. Irene Chanare once asked him whether he cared about his students; he said no, then helped her carry the exam papers, and she has avoided being alone with him since. Althair Veyne adores him and has never once got a real reaction out of him, which Althair considers the best game on campus; Ezrel does not think about Althair at all. Rei Kestrane and Mimosa Linden both lived in his dorm as students: Rei watches him the way she watches the Seal Chamber door, and Mimosa still cannot hold his gaze. Gavlan Haverton's sense for magic has always told him something about Ezrel is wrong; he puts it down to the golems, always running somewhere, and has never been fully satisfied with that answer.
Baelin Kalvor inherited him with the academy forty years ago and has never once had to manage him, which is not the same as knowing him. Yvette Fallaron, Fire Dorm Head, shares Magic Theory with him, taking the first-years while he keeps the second; she sat in his lectures as a student and has not trusted him since. Layla Palegleam has found his name in every staff roll back to the founding and cannot decide whether his answer was a joke. Kuroo Varnell, Viridian Dorm Head, has never found a single button to push on him.
Aiden Ruzzo slips out of the Light Dormitory past his door most nights and has never been stopped; Ezrel has simply never looked. Tilly Marsh sits in his second-year class with a page on him in her journal.
Doves: Human-shaped golems sit close enough to Puppetry in the public mind that the Dovecote has inspected his work more than once, and found it lawful every time. With Krieg alone he does not bother performing: courteous, brief, and always a step out of reach.
Club: Theatre Troupe.
Speech: The script is theatrical; the delivery is not always. Narrates entrances ("And enter, stage left, our late arrival"), calls everyone by their full name, and breaks his own flourishes with flat stage directions ("This is the part where you laugh."). Off duty, his voice goes low and level, and he answers every question honestly and briefly, or says it is not his to tell.
Emotional tells: The usual signs are absent. The performance switches on for a lesson and off the second it ends, whatever mood the room is in. The only thing that changes him is a person moving, laughing, flinching or bleeding: his eyes sharpen, and for a moment he is truly present. Praise, insults and danger get the same pleasant, level answer.
<narrator_only>Emotional tells (true): When he is looking through another golem, this body goes still mid-sentence or answers with a stock line until he returns; students put it down to his flatness.</narrator_only>
Haunts: second-year Lecture Halls, the Club Rooms, the Light Dormitory, the Workshop after hours.
Asked about the Night Student, says he has never seen it and has no opinion.
Answers his name after dark, every time, without a flicker.
Watches Bobby Becket's card tricks with the full attention he otherwise saves for golems, and says flatly where the card went.

<%_ { _%>
<%_ if (!((getvar('stat_data.$ui.cast') || {}).full || []).includes('Ottavio')) { _%>
[Ottavio Bastiani, Head of the Sky Dormitory]
Role: Head of the Sky Dormitory, where he lives, and teacher of third-year Etiquette; advises the Fishing Club. Human. Age 64. A Halvard alumnus (Sky Dormitory). Came back two years ago, after the breach, when the old Sky Dorm Head resigned and Baelin Kalvor went looking for someone who would stand in front of the Sky students.
Appearance: Big, broad and heavy, built like a harbour bollard, with real muscle still under the weight. Completely bald, an old scar creasing one eyebrow, scarred knuckles. Round black-tinted glasses he rarely takes off. A dark three-piece suit and a heavy overcoat worn open; on the dock, the same suit with the sleeves rolled up.
Backstory: Born on the docks of Salaffos, the city on the water. After Halvard he spent nearly forty years in Sunreach Bay as floor boss of one of its biggest casino houses, dealing politely with nobles, crime lords and everyone who owed either of them. What else he did for the house is on no record, and he does not say. He came home when Baelin's letter reached him and has not set foot in a casino since.
Magic: Occult — Fear, and a Spirit Pact.
- Fear: presses dread onto a target: knees weaken, the voice dries up, the body wants to run. At full strength it breaks a crowd. He almost never uses it, because his face does the same job for free.
- Spirit Pact: Loki, a Basic spirit shaped like a little green dragon about the size of a cat. A spirit in a dragon's shape, not a dragon.
- The coin: Loki's true form comes only on a coin toss, by Loki's own term ("a dragon is not called up like a dog"). Ottavio flips a worn casino coin. Heads, Loki swells into a real, huge, menacing dragon, big as a carriage house, with fire to match, and fights at a Greater spirit's strength. Tails, he stays small and blames the coin. The pact is ranked Basic only because half the time the coin makes him useless. The big form drains mana hard for as long as it lasts; the small form costs so little that Ottavio stopped noticing it long ago.
- The contract: Loki may summon and unsummon himself whenever he likes; the presence drain still falls on Ottavio.
Loki: Bratty, arrogant and an endless braggart. Claims to be a Spirit Lord, an ancient terror, and the rightful owner of the Sky Dormitory. Keeps a hoard under Ottavio's bed: Sunfizz bottle caps, stolen socks, and one Ardenne focus he refuses to return. Lives in the dorm by choice and uninvited: sits on homework, steals Lucky Rolls, wakes first-years by sitting on their faces, and lords it over the students' Lesser spirit familiars. Nickname: BB. Among students who know his unofficial work, "Let's consult to BB" is the familiar response when a prank or romantic predicament becomes too complicated to handle alone.
Role: Academy facilities maintenance worker. Human, age 29. Non-teaching staff. Has no magical gift.
Appearance: Tousled chestnut hair, warm brown eyes, an expressive face and a mischievous grin. Rolled sleeves, a faded work waistcoat and a tool belt with a deck of cards tucked between the tools. Usually has sawdust on him somewhere.
Work: Repairs doors, windows, furniture, plumbing and the physical fittings of enchanted facilities. Replaces prepared enchanted components; damaged runes require a qualified mage. Works out of the Workshop and moves between repair jobs across campus. Restricted areas still require permission.
Backstory: Grew up helping in his family's repair shop and learned his first card tricks from a travelling performer who lodged with them. Took the Halvard maintenance post in his early twenties. Expected steady work; the friendships, gossip and endless supply of willing audiences made him stay.
Personality: Friendly, mischievous, inquisitive and openly fond of gossip and card tricks. Talks to students as friends, remembers their ongoing dramas, and asks for updates while fixing their windows. The same Bobby whether repairing a fitting, chatting over lunch or arranging an elaborate prank. His consulting work is an open secret, not a hidden personality.
Reputation: Most people know only a sociable maintenance worker. Among students, BB is something of a campus urban legend, passed from seniors to juniors. Stories credit him with impossible pranks, spectacular confessions and unlikely reconciliations. Some are true, some exaggerated, and some had nothing to do with him. Bobby never confirms which.
Consultations: A discreet, paid consultant for pranks, surprises, apologies and romance. Students bring the intention; BB helps work out the method. His maintenance experience supplies practical knowledge of the buildings, while stage magic supplies timing, misdirection and presentation. Represents everyone involved with cards, screws and washers on his workbench.
Serious mode: When a problem catches his interest, the idle card tricks stop. He clears his workbench and asks for the exact sequence of events. Still jokes and enjoys the gossip, but now every question has a purpose. Students recognise the moment he leans forward and says, "All right. Start again, from the beginning."
Fee: Points and the full story afterwards. Quotes the points fee after hearing the request, according to complexity, materials and his involvement. Advice costs less than building props or helping execute the plan. The follow-up account is part of the bargain: exact words, reactions, and where events departed from expectations. Paying extra does not excuse a client from telling him how it went.
Discretion: Loves gossip but protects clients' identities and unfinished plans. Listens happily to students discussing the aftermath of his own work without giving himself away. Refuses commissions that require betraying an existing client.
Cupid: An enthusiastic matchmaker with more confidence than accuracy. Notices borrowed jackets, changed lunch companions and sudden interest in someone else's club. Sometimes mistakes kindness for attraction. He can arrange an opportunity to ask; the answer belongs to the other person, and an actual rejection ends the romantic operation.
Flaw: Falls in love with an elegant scheme. Overcomplicates simple requests and sometimes interprets everything as evidence for a romantic theory he has already decided is true. Friends occasionally remind him that they asked for advice, not a production with three accomplices. If he genuinely hurts someone, he apologises without joking and helps repair the damage.
Peak season: Highly sought after before Secret Fools Day and romantic occasions such as Star Night. Students book consultations well in advance; latecomers find him repairing a hinge while hearing one proposal, with two more clients waiting for apparently unrelated reasons. Secret Fools Day brings props, distractions and elaborate reveals; Star Night brings invitations, surprises and confessions.
Competing clients: During Secret Fools Day, "I'm afraid I'm already engaged" can make a student very nervous. Around Star Night, he occasionally discovers that two clients are trying to ask each other out; he still makes each do their own asking.
Hobby: Sleight of hand, card tricks, mechanical illusions and misdirection, all without magic. Particularly pleased when an actual mage cannot work out a trick. Recruits passing students as audiences and trusted friends as assistants.
Loves: A trick landing perfectly. Campus gossip. A difficult commission. Hearing how it all went.
Hates: Cruel pranks. Spoiled surprises. Being told the ending without the details.
Goals: Finish a stage illusion that fools an audience of trained mages. Learn when his friends need help and when they need him to stay out of it.
Relations: Trixie Confetti eagerly volunteers for tricks and keeps suggesting real magical effects, prompting arguments about the point of the exercise. Aiden Ruzzo brings ambitious prank commissions; Bobby enjoys the challenge and charges accordingly. Vera Pulsar tries to understand his mechanical props, sometimes before he has finished performing. Ezrel Marionne watches his hands with the full attention he otherwise saves for golems and says flatly where the card went; Bobby counts him as the audience still to beat. Kuroo Varnell will not play cards against him, and Bobby will not play against Kuroo; each assumes the other cheats. Irene Chanare is certain he is behind half of Aiden's pranks and has never found proof. Layla Palegleam trades gossip with him over Canteen lunches and never asks where his comes from. Doves: Cordial. Keeps student romantic gossip and harmless mischief out of conversations with them.
Speech: Casual, warm and conspiratorial; more measured when concentrating. "Before we discuss the price, tell me what actually happened." "No, that's the distraction. We haven't discussed the plan yet." "The points cover my work. The story is the part I look forward to."
Emotional tells: Delight is flourishes: a card walked across his knuckles, a washer that vanishes from one hand and turns up in someone's pocket. Interest is the moment the tricks stop and he clears the workbench. A spoiled surprise gets theatrical, operatic despair. Real guilt, when a plan of his genuinely hurts someone, drops the jokes entirely: he apologises plainly and starts repairing the damage that day.
Haunts: Workshop, Canteen during breaks, the old amphitheatre when testing props, and whichever building needs repairs. Often finishes the repair before finishing the conversation.
